scale: 0 absent, 1 mentioned without mechanism or uncommitted, 2 works but generic, 3 matches the reference architect's decision for the right reason, 4 also avoids the named known weakness

levels.2: Builds or adopts something with some rationale
levels.3: Argues build/extend/adopt from the facts (Jenkins plugin debt, one part-time maintainer, agent needs, 2 engineers / 3 months) and states explicit non-goals that keep it small
levels.4: Also states the production bill (durable state, identity/auth, retention, upgrades, on-call) as part of the go/no-go and scopes the first release to it

levels.3: Derives concurrent task slots and peak demand from 80 builds/h x 8-15 tasks x minutes vs 4x16 vCPU, accounts for agent retry multiplier and cache sizes on 500 GB disks
levels.4: Also sets admission control / per-identity limits from that arithmetic

levels.3: Control plane (webhooks, pipeline parsing, DAG, scheduling, state) separated from workers; one contract style; agent interface (API/MCP) as a client of the same API; domain separated from infrastructure
levels.4: Also avoids a single in-memory master as source of truth (state store owned by one component)

dimensions.name: Execution model: DAG, scheduling, workspace and caches

levels.3: Pipeline as code in repo, DAG with depends_on, cycle detection, skip cascade; resource-aware scheduling; shared per-build workspace; persistent dependency caches across builds
levels.4: Also handles cache eviction/TTL and pipeline-level timeouts or label-based routing

levels.3: Worker heartbeats, task timeouts, idempotent task execution and retry semantics defined
levels.4: Build state persisted (survives control-plane restart) and tasks on dead workers reassigned automatically, in the turn-1 design

levels.3: Agent-facing tools for submit/watch/logs/structured failure diagnosis/retry-failed-only, paginated logs
levels.4: Also structured failure events (not regex over text), per-task re-run reusing unchanged upstream outputs, or a cost/budget stop signal for agent loops

levels.3: HMAC webhook verification, secrets injected at runtime and scrubbed from logs and agent output, mTLS/auth between components
levels.4: Also per-human/per-agent identity with audit, and stronger-than-Docker isolation for untrusted agent code

levels.3: Integrations (linters/scanners/review) added via a registry/plugin into the DAG without scheduler changes; SCM providers and container runtime behind interfaces
levels.4: Also keeps extension points to the named axes only (no plugin marketplace)

levels.3: Metrics for builds/queue/workers incl. agent share; structured logs; worker draining
levels.4: Also log/build retention, graceful upgrade, backup/restore

levels.2: Adds persistence or reassignment or identity, not all
levels.3: All three: durable state store as source of truth with recovery of in-flight builds, automatic reassignment with idempotent re-execution, per-identity tokens with attribution and quotas
levels.4: Also updates the affected earlier sections consistently (scheduler, API, audit, agent loop budget) and names what the change costs

penalties.name: Unjustified heavy infrastructure (Kubernetes, service mesh, message bus, microservices per component) for 5 VMs and 2 engineers
Plans Jenkins feature parity (plugin ecosystem, rich UI, multi-platform) within the stated team and timeline
Secrets visible to untrusted pipeline code or agent output without mitigation
